title_en: Koreans don't say hi. They ask if you ate. #shorts
description_en: In Korea, "bap meogeosseo?" (Did you eat?) is an everyday greeting between friends. Learn what it means and how to answer.
hook_vi: Ở Hàn Quốc, "Ăn cơm chưa?" nghĩa là "Xin chào."
hook_pt: Na Coreia, «Você já comeu?» quer dizer «Oi».
hook_fil: Sa Korea, ang «Kumain ka na?» ay «Hi» lang.
hook_voice: In Korea, did you eat, means hi.

scenes.voice: Korean friends often greet you with: bap meogeosseo? Did you eat?

scenes.vi: Anh chị đã ăn cơm chưa ạ? (lịch sự)
scenes.voice: Many say it comes from harder times, when asking if someone ate meant: are you okay? To older people, say: siksa hasyeosseoyo?
You don't need to explain your lunch. Just say: eung, meogeosseo!

cta.en: Let's grab a meal sometime! (Next time: is it a real invite?)
cta.vi: Bữa nào đi ăn nhé! (Lần sau: có phải lời mời thật không?)
cta.id: Kapan-kapan makan bareng ya! (Berikutnya: ajakan beneran?)
cta.es: ¡Comamos juntos algún día! (¿Es una invitación de verdad?)
cta.pt: Vamos comer juntos qualquer dia! (É convite de verdade?)
cta.ar: لنتناول الطعام معًا يومًا ما! (هل هي دعوة حقيقية؟)
cta.fil: Kain tayo minsan! (Totoo ba ang imbitasyon?)
cta.voice: Next time: is bap hanbeon meokja a real invitation? Follow for one Korean phrase a day.
